## TL;DR – What you need now | Item | UK GDPR (DPA 2018) | EU GDPR | Divergence | Documentation you must create | |------|-------------------|---------|------------|--------------------------------| | **Lawful basis for *processing* HR data** | • Art. 6(1)(b) – “necessary for the performance of a contract” (employment).
• Art. 6(1)(f) – legitimate interest (managing staff, statutory obligations).
• Art. 9(2)(j) – compliance with legal or regulatory obligations (health‑data). | Same bases (Art. 6 & 9). | None – both mirror each other. | • Updated *Record of Processing Activities*.
• Internal policy stating the chosen basis for each HR function. | | **Lawful basis for *transfer* to Germany** | • Art. 44‑50 DPA: Transfer is allowed only if the destination has an adequacy decision **or** “appropriate safeguards” are in place (SCCs, BCR).
• Germany is a *third country* after Brexit – you must rely on a UK‑SCC or BCR. | • Art. 44‑50 GDPR: intra‑EU transfer is automatically adequate; only the processor’s contractual commitments matter.
• No extra safeguards required beyond those already in place for EU‑to‑EU transfers. | **Adequacy** – UK has *none* for Germany; EU does not need one.
**SCC text** – UK SCC includes a “right‑to‑complaint” clause that can be lodged with any supervisory authority, whereas the EU SCC allows complaints in either country. | • Processor Data Processing Agreement (DPA) must contain the **UK Standard Contractual Clauses (UK‑SCC)**.
• If you already use the EU SCC, replace it with the UK version and add a “transformation” clause if you pseudonymise data before transfer. | | **Special category (health) data** | • Must have an explicit lawful basis (usually Art. 9(2)(j)).
• Requires a Data Protection Impact Assessment (DPIA) if processing poses high risks. | Same requirement – DPIA or at least a risk assessment for special categories. | None – both require a DPIA, but the UK DPA’s guidance is stricter on *transformation* and *key custody*. | • **DPIA** covering HR health data.
• Technical documentation of encryption & key‑management (UK‑controlled keys). | | **Data‑subject rights & complaints** | • Under Art. 34 & UK DPA – employees can lodge a complaint with any supervisory authority, and the processor must cooperate. | • Same right, but the EU SCC gives more flexibility in where complaints may be lodged. | The UK SCC has a *specific* “right to complain” clause that points to **any** supervisory authority; the EU SCC is more permissive. | • Add a *Data‑Subject Rights Schedule* to the DPA.
• Update employee privacy notice to explain the rights and how to exercise them. | | **Enforcement landscape (2024‑26)** | • ICO has issued “Transfer‑Safeguards” guidance – SCCs must be *operationally compliant*; otherwise they are ineffective.
• Potential fines: up to £5 m for non‑compliance or a breach during transfer. | • EDPB Opinions (2023‑24) and *Schrems III* keep tightening the use of SCCs – a Transfer Impact Assessment is mandatory even for intra‑EU special‑category data.
• GDPR fines: up to €20 m (€≈£17 m). | The UK is increasingly demanding evidence that the processor actually implements the safeguards; EU authorities are applying the same scrutiny. | • **Transfer Impact Assessment** (for UK, optional but recommended for audit).
• **Audit trail & SIEM logs** to prove compliance.
• **Contractual SLA clauses** covering breach notification and penalties. | --- ## The “Processor’s Migration Window” | Stage | Duration | What it covers | Why it matters | |-------|----------|----------------|----------------| | **Full migration of data** | **6 weeks** (processor‑quoted) | Transfer of all employee records, including health fields, from the UK system to the German processor. | Missing this window triggers a *Service Level Agreement* penalty and increases the risk that a breach will be detected while the data is in transit. | | **Overall project timeline** | **14 weeks** (project‑wide) | 8 weeks of preparation (DPIA, legal review, technical set‑up), 6 weeks of migration, 1–2 weeks for post‑migration testing & audit. | The 6‑week window sits inside a longer project; you must budget for the full 14 weeks and keep contingency funds ready for any delay that spills into the critical transfer period. | --- ## What to Prepare – A Checklist | Document | Who prepares it? | Why it is required | Key content | |----------|------------------|-------------------|--------------| | **Updated Data Processing Agreement (DPA)** | Legal & Compliance teams, in coordination with the processor | Governs the transfer and ensures that UK‑SCC clauses are present; includes data‑subject rights, breach notification, audit rights. | • UK SCC text
• Lawful basis clause for special category data
• Sub‑processor list and approval process
• Right‑to‑complaint provision | | **Transfer Impact Assessment (TIA)** | Data Protection Officer (DPO) / Compliance team | Demonstrates that the transfer meets “appropriate safeguards” under UK law. Not required for intra‑EU but useful for audit trails. | • Description of data flows, volumes & categories
• Safeguards applied (SCCs, encryption)
• Risk mitigation plan | | **Data Protection Impact Assessment (DPIA)** | DPO / Privacy team | Required for high‑risk processing of health data; shows that the company has considered re‑identification, aggregation risks, etc. | • Purpose & necessity
• Lawful basis
• Technical & organisational measures (encryption, access control)
• Balancing test for legitimate interest | | **Record of Processing Activities** | Data Governance team | Mandatory under Art. 30 DPA/GDPR; must list processors in Germany and the data they handle. | • Processor name & contact
• Categories of personal data (including special categories)
• Purpose & lawful basis | | **Privacy Notice / Employee Communication** | HR & Legal | Informed‑consent requirement for special category data transfer; also satisfies Art. 13/14 DPA/GDPR. | • What data is transferred, why, where
• Rights employees have (access, rectification, complaint)
• Contact details of the controller and DPO | | **Technical Architecture Diagram** | IT & Security teams | Provides evidence that encryption, key‑management, network segmentation etc. are in place. | • End‑to‑end encryption (TLS 1.3/VPN)
• UK‑controlled KMS or on‑premise key store
• RBAC / MFA controls | | **Audit & Log Evidence** | IT Operations | Proof that access is logged, monitored, and that only authorised personnel see the data during migration. | • SIEM dashboards, log retention policy
• Access logs for the 6‑week window | | **Contingency & Penalty Schedule** | Finance & Legal | Pre‑pays penalties if SLA breaches occur; also allocates a buffer for unforeseen costs. | • 10–20 % contingency reserve (≈£30–40 k)
• SLA penalty per week of delay (e.g., £30 k/week) | | **Insurance Endorsement** | Risk Management | Cyber‑insurance must cover “in‑transit” data breach risks. | • Endorsement for migration period
• Coverage limits and exclusions | --- ## Enforcement & What the Regulators Are Watching 1. **ICO – Transfer‑Safeguards Guidance (2025)** * ICO now tests that processors truly implement the UK SCCs, not just sign them. Evidence of encryption, key custody, audit logs is required. A failure can trigger a £17 m fine. 2. **EDPB Opinions 2023/24** * Re‑affirmed that even intra‑EU transfers of special categories must have a Transfer Impact Assessment and robust safeguards. Non‑compliance can lead to €20 m fines. 3. **Schrems III (CJEU, 2025)** * Clarified that “adequacy” is not a blanket exemption; each transfer must be justified by specific safeguards. This means the UK SCC must be operationally effective. 4. **UK DPA Enforcement** * The ICO has begun to issue penalties for non‑compliant transfers, especially where employee health data are involved. Penalties can reach £5 m or 2 % of turnover. --- ## Bottom Line | What you must do | Why it matters | How soon | |------------------|----------------|----------| | **Replace the EU SCC with a UK SCC in the DPA** | Germany is now a third country; only UK‑SCCs (or BCR) are legal. | Before the 6‑week migration window starts. | | **Complete a DPIA for all health data** | Health records are special category data and high‑risk. | At least 4 weeks before migration. | | **Prepare a Transfer Impact Assessment** | Demonstrates that safeguards meet UK law; required by ICO. | 2–3 weeks before migration. | | **Document encryption & key custody in the UK** | Prevents loss of control over keys and potential breaches. | Ongoing, but evidence must be ready for audit at the end of the 6‑week window. | | **Set up a log‑and‑monitoring system that captures every access during migration** | Enables rapid breach detection & satisfies Art. 33/34 notification timelines. | Within 1 week of migration start. | | **Allocate a contingency reserve (10–20 %) and prepare for SLA penalties** | Protects the budget from cost overruns or delayed transfer. | Immediately, as part of project budgeting. | By following this checklist you’ll satisfy both UK and EU requirements, minimise enforcement risk, and keep the 6‑week migration window on track within the overall 14‑week project timeline.
